Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: This is an initial broad, biologically motivated wave focusing on high-prior binary predictors that are likely to show meaningful associations with CRISPR dependency scores. More negative dependency means stronger dependence, so claims with direction -1 expect a more negative score in the exposed group, whereas direction +1 expects a less negative/positive score. I prioritize canonical oncogene-dependency relationships: KRAS mutation with KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency, and ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2 dependency. I also test whether KRAS mutation extends to nearby RAS-pathway dependency on RIT1. Synthetic-lethality and pathway-specific hypotheses are included: MDM2 and USP7 dependencies should be weaker in TP53-loss lines because p53-proficient cells are typically more sensitive to p53 regulators; WRN dependency should be stronger in MSI-high lines; NFE2L2 dependency should be stronger in KEAP1-loss lines because KEAP1 loss activates the NRF2/NFE2L2 axis; SMARCA2 dependency should be stronger in SMARCA4-deficient lines due to SWI/SNF paralog dependence. Finally, MYC amplification is tested as a marker of transcriptional addiction, with predicted stronger DHX9 and POLR2A dependencies. These analyses will identify which predictor-outcome pairs are worth focused follow-up; later waves can assess research signatures, marker assays, culture/library effects, and interaction/subgroup refinements.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The independent validation for H3 does not support EGFR amplification as a meaningful predictor of EGFR dependency in this dataset. The discovery signed estimate was +0.0252 (95% interval -0.00025 to +0.0507), barely favoring stronger dependency but not excluding no effect. The validation signed estimate was -0.0221 (independent interval -0.0614 to +0.0172), i.e. the opposite direction, while still including no effect. The two estimates are not consistent, and the magnitude is small relative to the 10% clinical-significance benchmark; therefore H3 is rejected as a supported association. The large discovery effects for H7, H8, H10, and the reversed NFE2L2/KEAP1 relationship H13 remain accepted as dataset-level associations. H13 is now accepted because, when the direction was reversed from the original biological hypothesis, the same direct evidence shows a very large and precise effect: KEAP1-loss lines have much weaker NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-intact lines (signed estimate +0.796, 95% interval +0.776 to +0.816). This is a post hoc direction correction based on the observed data, but the effect is far beyond the 10% benchmark and far from null; it is still only an observational association in this cell-line dataset, not causal proof. For the accepted large effects, the main uncertainties are confounding and generalizability: lineage subtype, co-occurring TP53/KEAP1/MSI/SMARCA4 states, culture or library artifacts, and research-marker assay effects could explain or modify them. The next wave therefore prioritizes (1) replication of the four large associations within adenocarcinoma, (2) interaction tests asking whether adenocarcinoma versus complement differ, (3) co-occurrence checks by restricting each exposure to lines without the other major predictor, and (4) research-marker/library controls to detect nonbiological driver patterns. If these robustness and negative-control analyses do not reveal technical artifacts, independent validation can be used sparingly on one of the accepted large effects, but the most immediate informative work is subgroup/co-mutation decomposition rather than more borderline single-marker tests.

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: The first wave supports four very large dataset-level associations: KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, TP53 loss with much weaker USP7 dependency, SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and MSI-high status with much stronger WRN dependency. Before treating these as broadly meaningful or interpretable, I want to determine whether they are robust to the strongest plausible confounders and whether they are predictor-specific. The first four new proposals replicate each accepted effect in lines lacking the other major genetic states: NFE2L2 in TP53-intact/MSS lines, USP7 in KEAP1-intact/MSS lines, SMARCA2 in TP53-intact/KEAP1-intact/MSS lines, and WRN in TP53-intact/KEAP1-intact lines. If these co-occurrence-restricted estimates remain large and directional, they are less likely to be driven only by co-mutation mixture. The library-Avana controls and marker controls test whether the large dependencies are artifacts of screen batch/library or constructed marker assays; for these controls I use the signed direction matching the accepted association for that outcome, so a large positive signed effect would raise concern about a shared technical or latent cell-state driver. The interaction controls test whether the accepted genetic effects differ within marker-defined subgroups, again probing artifact or modification. The cross-pathway specificity tests ask whether KEAP1 loss also moves USP7 and whether SMARCA4 loss also moves WRN; strong cross-effects would suggest a non-specific latent factor rather than pathway-specific dependence. I am not requesting validation yet: validation is more useful after these robustness and artifact screens, and should be reserved for associations that remain large and stable.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

record.narrative:
The co-occurrence-restricted replication is very informative. H29 keeps the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 result within lines that are TP53-intact and MSS: KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, signed estimate +0.795, 95% interval +0.771 to +0.818. H30 similarly preserves the TP53/USP7 association among KEAP1-intact, MSS lines, signed estimate +0.802, interval +0.779 to +0.826. H31 preserves the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 association among TP53-intact, KEAP1-intact, MSS lines, signed estimate +0.784, interval +0.759 to +0.808. H32 preserves the MSI-high/WRN association among TP53-intact and KEAP1-intact lines, signed estimate +0.774, interval +0.736 to +0.813, despite a smaller exposed cell_n of 81. These restricted estimates are all far larger than the 10% clinical-significance benchmark and show that the accepted large associations are not simple proxies for one another or limited to lines containing the other major genetic state. They still remain observational cell-line associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

The artifact and specificity screens are reassuring. The dominant CRISPR library indicator is not associated with large outcome shifts in the same signed direction as the accepted claims: H20 WRN versus Avana estimate -0.022, H33 NFE2L2 estimate +0.036, H34 SMARCA2 estimate +0.051, and H35 USP7 estimate +0.046; all intervals include zero and point estimates are small relative to the accepted effects of roughly 0.78-0.80. The upper bound for H34 slightly exceeds 0.10, but the non-significant point is modest and does not resemble the magnitude of the accepted SMARCA4/SMARCA2 effect. Constructed markers are not strong direct drivers: H18 SMARCA2 versus marker F estimate -0.015 and H36 NFE2L2 versus marker E estimate +0.001, both with intervals near zero. Cross-pathway specificity is also consistent with pathway-specific associations: H41 KEAP1 loss versus USP7 estimate +0.009 and H42 SMARCA4 loss versus WRN estimate +0.003 are small and non-directional. I reject these negative-control and cross-effect claims as scientifically meaningful associations and close them. These controls do not prove absence of technical confounding; they mainly show that no direct marker or library effect of comparable magnitude was detected. Residual confounding through correlated library/genotype distributions, batch, culture conditions, or other latent states remains possible.

Given that the large associations have now passed direct artifact screens and co-occurrence robustness checks, I request independent validation for H13, the KEAP1-loss/weaker-NFE2L2-dependency association. This is the most consequential unresolved issue because it required a reversal of the original biological hypothesis and because post hoc direction reversal deserves independent confirmation. If validation reproduces a positive signed effect, H13 becomes a more credible dataset-level association. If validation does not reproduce it, H13 should be downgraded and the subgroup/interaction analyses will become the priority. I selected H13 rather than H7, H8, or H10 for this validation slot because H13 is the most surprising and most likely to be affected by dataset-specific structure.

references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The independent validation for H13 strongly supports the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 association. H13 was registered after the original H9 hypothesis was contradicted by discovery data, so this is a post hoc directional claim; however, the validation now confirms it. The validation signed estimate is +0.806 with an independent interval of +0.775 to +0.838, excluding zero under a stringent validation threshold and far exceeding the 10% clinical-significance benchmark. Because dependency scores are more negative when dependency is stronger, a positive signed estimate under direction +1 means KEAP1-loss lines have much less negative NFE2L2 scores, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency. This is consistent with the discovery estimate of +0.796 and with the co-occurrence-restricted estimate of +0.795 in TP53-intact/MSS lines. I therefore accept H13 as a scientifically meaningful dataset-level association, while H9 remains rejected because the same evidence confirms the opposite of its original expected stronger NFE2L2 dependency. The current evidence base now separates three layers: validated broad association, accepted but not independently validated associations, and negative/artifact controls. The accepted broad effects are H13 KEAP1 loss associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, H7 TP53 loss associated with weaker USP7 dependency, H8 MSI-high associated with stronger WRN dependency, and H10 SMARCA4 loss associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Their restricted robustness claims H29-H32 also remain accepted, with estimated effects of roughly +0.77 to +0.80 even after excluding lines with the other major genetic states. The artifact screens did not support a large marker-F, marker-E, library-Avana, or cross-pathway effect: H18, H36, H20, H33-H35, H41, and H42 are rejected as meaningful associations. H3 is also a clear negative finding: EGFR amplification had a borderline positive discovery effect but opposite validation effect, so the evidence does not support EGFR amplification as a meaningful predictor of EGFR dependency in this dataset. Remaining uncertainty is mainly generalizability and residual confounding rather than effect size for the accepted effects: H7, H8, and H10 still lack independent validation, and all four accepted effects could still be modified by lineage subtype, screen batch, culture condition, age, sex, or other latent cell-state variables. The most informative next analysis is therefore the remaining robustness and interaction panel: lineage-specific replication in adenocarcinoma, Avana versus non-Avana robustness, batch-a interaction tests, marker interaction/main controls, and pathway-inspired specificity tests such as ARID1A loss with SMARCA2 dependency and TP53 loss with RPL11 dependency. If these subgroup tests remain broadly consistent, the next validation request should target one canonical accepted effect, likely H10 SMARCA4 loss associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; if heterogeneity is large, interaction analysis should take priority over additional validation.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: Selecting twelve new analyses to interrogate robustness, heterogeneity, and pathway specificity of the four accepted large associations. First, H25-H28 request interaction tests by lineage subtype (adenocarcinoma vs complement) for SMARCA2/SMARCA4, WRN/MSI, USP7/TP53, and NFE2L2/KEAP1. These ask whether the accepted effects differ by subtype or are homogeneous across the measured subtype split. Because estimates are already signed to the hypothesis direction, a positive signed interaction would indicate the effect is stronger in adenocarcinoma than in the complement, whereas a negative signed interaction would indicate it is weaker. Second, H52-H55 request analogous screen_batch_a interactions for the same four accepted associations, testing whether a dominant technical/batch variable modifies the effects. Third, H56-H58 are co-mutation-restricted main effects: KEAP1-loss effect on NFE2L2 among TP53-loss lines, TP53-loss effect on USP7 among KEAP1-loss lines, and SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 among TP53-loss lines. These complement the earlier TP53/KEAP1/MSS-restricted tests and ask whether the effects persist when the exposure is considered within the presence of another major genetic state rather than only in lines lacking it. Fourth, H47 tests ARID1A loss versus SMARCA2 dependency as a BAF-complex specificity check: if ARID1A loss produces a comparable SMARCA2 shift, the association may reflect general SWI/SNF/BAF loss biology; if it does not, the SMARCA4-specific association remains more specific. I defer sex, culture, serum, marker, and other broad pathway tests until these heterogeneity and specificity screens clarify whether the accepted effects are stable enough to merit further validation.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The new interaction and conditional-effect panel largely supports the stability of the four accepted large associations while identifying one small, statistically detectable but clinically trivial batch interaction. For lineage subtype, all interaction estimates are close to zero and below the practical clinical-significance scale: H25 SMARCA4/SMARCA2 estimate -0.028 [-0.076, 0.020]; H26 MSI/WRN -0.021 [-0.085, 0.042]; H27 TP53/USP7 -0.010 [-0.053, 0.033]; H28 KEAP1/NFE2L2 -0.012 [-0.057, 0.033]. I therefore reject these lineage-subtype interaction claims as meaningful subgroup modifications. This does not prove complete homogeneity, but it gives no support for the accepted effects being driven only by adenocarcinoma versus the complement.  The screen-batch_a interactions are also small. H52 KEAP1/NFE2L2 +0.021 [-0.031, 0.072], H53 TP53/USP7 -0.019 [-0.064, 0.027], and H55 MSI/WRN +0.048 [-0.020, 0.115] have point estimates far below the 10%-or-0.1-scale benchmark and confidence intervals centered near zero. H54 SMARCA4/SMARCA2 is different in that its interval excludes zero, signed estimate -0.051 [-0.095, -0.007], but the magnitude is still small: it corresponds to a modest, opposite-signed batch modification and is only about 6% of the main SMARCA4/SMARCA2 effect. With many subgroup tests, I interpret this as statistically detectable but not clinically meaningful heterogeneity, and I reject it as a meaningful interaction.  The co-mutation-restricted main effects are very informative. H56, the KEAP1-loss effect on NFE2L2 dependency among TP53-loss lines, is strongly positive, signed estimate +0.810 [0.763, 0.857]; because the signed direction is +1, this indicates much weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines even when TP53 is lost. H57, the TP53-loss effect on USP7 dependency among KEAP1-loss lines, is also large, +0.794 [0.754, 0.834], supporting weaker USP7 dependency in TP53-loss lines within KEAP1-loss contexts. H58, the SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 dependency among TP53-loss lines, is strong, +0.773 [0.729, 0.817], consistent with stronger SMARCA2 dependency in SMARCA4-loss lines. These conditional effects are all far larger than the clinical benchmark and indicate that the accepted effects are not limited to lines lacking another major genetic state. They remain observational dataset-level associations, not causal effects.  The pathway-specificity check H47 rejects ARID1A loss as an alternative broad BAF-complex explanation for the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 association: signed estimate -0.017 [-0.057, 0.023]. Since ARID1A loss is not associated with SMARCA2 dependency of comparable magnitude, the accepted SMARCA4/SMARCA2 effect remains more specific to SMARCA4 loss than to generalized BAF loss.  Overall, this panel strengthens confidence in the accepted effects: no lineage interaction is clinically meaningful; batch effects are mostly negligible, with one small SMARCA4/SMARCA2 modification; co-mutation-restricted effects remain very large; and an ARID1A control does not reproduce the SMARCA2 effect. I therefore request independent validation for H10, the SMARCA4-loss association with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, because it is canonical, pathway-specific, and now supported by direct co-occurrence and specificity checks. This validation will not establish causality or generalizability, but it would materially strengthen the dataset-level evidence.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

The next wave is organized around three complementary goals. First, I registered conditional follow-ups for the accepted large associations in the presence of another major genetic state: KEAP1-loss effect on NFE2L2 within TP53-loss lines, TP53-loss effect on USP7 within KEAP1-loss lines, and SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 within TP53-loss lines. These ask whether the accepted effects persist in alternative co-mutation contexts rather than only in lines that lack the other major state. Second, I registered robustness and interaction tests using measurable technical and demographic subgroups that have not yet been interrogated: high screen ROC quality for KEAP1/NFE2L2, male sex for TP53/USP7, adherent culture for SMARCA4/SMARCA2, and high serum for MSI/WRN. These test whether the very large associations are generalized across screen quality, sex, culture configuration, and medium serum, or whether they are driven or modified by these subgroup factors. Third, I registered cross-pathway specificity controls: TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss with SMARCA2, and SMARCA4-loss with USP7. record.narrative:
The independent validation of H10 is decisive. The signed validation estimate is +0.7925 with an independent interval of +0.763 to +0.822. Because H10 was registered with direction -1, a positive signed estimate corresponds to a negative exposed-minus-comparator difference in raw dependency units, i.e. SMARCA4-loss lines have substantially more negative SMARCA2 scores than SMARCA4-intact lines. Since more negative scores mean stronger CRISPR dependency, this confirms that SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency in this dataset. The effect is far larger than the practical 10%-scale benchmark and is consistent with the discovery estimate (+0.784) and with restricted co-occurrence analyses (e.g., +0.784 in TP53/KEAP1/MSS lines and +0.773 among TP53-loss lines). I therefore accept H10 as a scientifically meaningful dataset-level association and close it as a canonical validated result. This does not establish causality or external generalizability, but it strengthens the dataset-level association. H10 is now independently validated alongside H13.

The H3 response deadline is also clear. Discovery gave a small signed estimate favoring EGFR amplification -> stronger EGFR dependency, but the validation estimate was opposite-signed and small (-0.022, interval -0.061 to +0.017). Across both discovery and validation the magnitude is well below the practical clinical-significance threshold and the evidence is inconsistent. Therefore EGFR amplification is not supported as a meaningful predictor of EGFR dependency in this dataset, and H3 remains rejected.

The next most informative work is not additional validation of the already validated canonical associations, but robustness across technical strata and screen quality, plus one leakage check for pathway specificity. I am keeping active the Avana-library effects for USP7/TP53, SMARCA2/SMARCA4, WRN/MSI, and NFE2L2/KEAP1; the non-Avana main effects for NFE2L2, USP7, and SMARCA2; a new non-Avana NFE2L2 effect; high screen-quality main effects for NFE2L2, USP7, SMARCA2, and WRN; and H63, which tests whether TP53 loss also shifts SMARCA2 dependency. I deferred lower-priority marker interactions, adenocarcinoma-only main effects because the corresponding lineage interactions were already small, sex/culture/serum interactions, other cross-specificity tests, and broad pathway discovery tests. This focused panel asks whether the large effects survive the dominant library split and high-quality screens, and whether they leak across pathways. After these results, the likely next validation target should be H8, MSI-high -> stronger WRN dependency, because its exposed cell size is smaller and independent validation would be most informative for a rare-subgroup synthetic-lethality-like association; H7 remains a secondary validation candidate.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No new discovery or validation evidence is due at this explore stage. The current evidence base strongly supports four dataset-level associations: KEAP1 loss associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (validated), SMARCA4 loss associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (validated), TP53 loss associated with weaker USP7 dependency, and MSI-high associated with stronger WRN dependency. The main remaining scientific questions are not whether these associations have large effects, but whether they are modified by major genetic co-states, screen-quality, or CRISPR library context, and whether they leak into biologically related dependencies. I therefore registered direct interaction tests rather than adding more subset main effects. First, I registered genetic-context interactions for the accepted effects: KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 modification by TP53-loss, TP53-loss/USP7 modification by KEAP1-loss, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 modification by TP53-loss, and MSI-high/WRN modification by TP53-loss. These are more direct than comparing separate conditional main effects and test whether the associations behave homogeneously across TP53 or KEAP1 co-mutation status. Second, I registered screen-quality interactions using screen_roc_auc >= 0.93 versus the complement for all four accepted associations. This tests whether high-quality screens show the same effect magnitude as lower-quality screens, which is relevant to technical reliability. Third, I registered Avana-library interactions for KEAP1/NFE2L2, TP53/USP7, and SMARCA4/SMARCA2. I did not register a WRN library interaction because MSI-high within non-Avana lines is expected to be too small for stable Welch cells; for WRN, the broad and screen-quality interactions are more informative than a fragile library-stratified test. I deferred the previously registered library and screen-quality main-effect strata because the new interaction tests are more direct and statistically efficient for assessing modification. I also deferred TP53-loss with RPL11 dependency to keep the immediate focus on robustness of the four accepted large associations and one leakage control (H63, TP53-loss with SMARCA2 dependency). record.narrative: These twelve new results are secondary heterogeneity and specificity tests for the four large accepted associations. Their signed effect sizes are small compared with the main effects: H76 KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 interaction by TP53 loss is +0.0176 [-0.0340, 0.0693]; H77 TP53-loss/USP7 interaction by KEAP1 loss is -0.0100 [-0.0562, 0.0361]; H78 SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 interaction by TP53 loss is -0.0145 [-0.0636, 0.0345]; and H79 MSI-high/WRN interaction by TP53 loss is +0.0528 [-0.0215, 0.1272], where the latter is imprecise because the MSI-high/TP53-loss cell has n=24. The screen-quality interactions are also small: H80 +0.0042 [-0.0412, 0.0497], H81 +0.0255 [-0.0212, 0.0723], H82 +0.0218 [-0.0250, 0.0685], and H83 +0.0126 [-0.0659, 0.0911]. The Avana-library interactions are similarly small: H84 +0.0022 [-0.0506, 0.0550], H85 +0.0383 [-0.0292, 0.1057], and H86 -0.0198 [-0.0762, 0.0365]. None provides statistically or clinically meaningful evidence of effect modification on the 0.1-scale dependency benchmark; where intervals are wider, the point estimates remain far below the main effects and the evidence is not significant. I therefore reject all interaction claims as meaningful subgroup modifications and close them. The leakage/specificity control H63 is essentially null: signed estimate -0.00057 [-0.0407, 0.0396]. TP53 loss is not associated with SMARCA2 dependency, so this rejects a broad shared cell-state or pathway leakage explanation and supports the specificity of the accepted TP53/USP7 and SMARCA4/SMARCA2 associations. Collectively, this panel strengthens confidence that the broad dataset-level effects for H7, H8, H10, and H13 are not driven by major genetic co-states, screen-quality, or the dominant CRISPR library split. These remain dataset-level associations, not causal or externally generalizable claims. Given the small exposed subgroup for MSI-high WRN and the robustness of its interactions, the most valuable next independent check is validation of H8.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation

initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: H13 response deadline is resolved decisively by independent validation. The signed validation estimate for KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 dependency is +0.8065 with an independent interval of +0.7754 to +0.8376. Because H13 is direction +1, this is a raw positive shift: KEAP1-loss lines have much more positive NFE2L2 scores, meaning substantially weaker dependency. The interval is tight, wholly away from zero and from any trivial range, and it matches discovery +0.7961 [0.7759, 0.8163]. I therefore keep H13 accepted and close it as a validated dataset-level association. H8 validation is equally decisive. The signed estimate for MSI-high on WRN dependency is +0.8019, independent interval +0.7533 to +0.8506. Because H8 is direction -1, a positive signed value corresponds to a raw negative shift: MSI-high lines have much more negative WRN scores, meaning much stronger WRN dependency. This is consistent with discovery +0.7899 [0.7604, 0.8193] and far exceeds the practical 10% clinical-significance benchmark. I therefore accept H8 as a scientifically meaningful, independently validated dataset-level association and close it. The earlier interaction panel showed no clinically meaningful modification by lineage, screen quality, library, or TP53/KEAP1 co-states for these large effects, and pathway-specificity controls did not suggest simple leakage. I am therefore moving from validating already-settled associations to broadening the search across remaining outcomes and plausible predictors. record.narrative: No new evidence is due, so the exploratory priority is to keep the immediate analysis budget focused on new, mechanistically plausible dependencies rather than further stratifying already-settled canonical effects. The validated dataset-level associations are KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency. H7 TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency remains the most important accepted association lacking independent validation, but validation is better considered after the new broad discovery panel returns because a newly discovered large association could become a more urgent validation target. To keep exactly twelve active comparisons for the next analyze stage, I defer two lower-priority TMED10 tests: TMED10 with EGFR amplification and TMED10 with PIK3CA mutation. EGFR amplification has already been weakly inconsistent for EGFR dependency, PIK3CA is still being tested for STAT3, and these TMED10 hypotheses are less mechanistically direct. I add two more focused comparisons. First, dependency_TMED10 by KRAS mutation: KRAS mutation is the dominant lung adenocarcinoma driver in this dataset, and TMED10 is a Golgi cargo-transport factor, so mutant KRAS lines may depend more strongly on secretory or membrane-traffic machinery. The expected raw contrast is more negative TMED10 dependency in KRAS-mutant versus wild-type lines, hence direction -1 and anticipated raw direction -1. Plausible alternatives are null if TMED10 is a general essential gene, or opposite if KRAS-mutant lines compensate through altered secretory traffic. Second, dependency_MDM2 by CDKN2A loss: CDKN2A encodes p14ARF as well as p16; ARF loss can enhance MDM2-mediated p53 control, so CDKN2A-loss lines may show stronger MDM2 dependency. The expected raw contrast is more negative MDM2 dependency in CDKN2A-loss lines, hence direction -1 and anticipated raw direction -1. Plausible alternatives are null if CDKN2A loss is dominated by p16 cell-cycle effects unrelated to MDM2, or opposite if CDKN2A loss co-occurs with TP53 loss and removes the MDM2-p53 dependency axis. These new tests remain exploratory and dataset-level. A clinically meaningful discovery would be a signed mean difference around 0.1 or larger with an interval away from zero; canonical effects are much larger, while small intervals near zero would support outcome or pathway specificity.

record.narrative: This analyze stage requests the twelve currently active, untested discovery comparisons that broaden the investigation to additional dependency outcomes while including specificity controls. The panel tests: RPL11 with TP53 loss; STAT3 with PIK3CA mutation, PTEN loss, and MYC amplification; KIF18A with RB1 loss, CDKN2A loss, and MYC amplification; TMED10 with ERBB2 amplification and KRAS mutation; MDM2 with CDKN2A loss; and DHX9/POLR2A with TP53 loss as specificity controls for the already-supported TP53-associated associations. These are selected because they cover plausible mechanistic axes: p53/RPL11 and p53/MDM2/ARF biology, PI3K/PTEN/MYC signaling with STAT3, cell-cycle/mitotic dependencies with RB1/CDKN2A/MYC and KIF18A, oncogenic driver/secretory traffic associations with KRAS/ERBB2 and TMED10, and transcriptional/RNA helicase controls with TP53. A meaningful positive finding would require an effect of at least roughly 0.1 dependency units with an interval away from zero, in line with the practical 10% benchmark; smaller or imprecise effects would be treated as null or unresolved rather than clinically meaningful. These remain dataset-level associations, not causal or generalizable claims.
